units.source_text: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

en.t: Shinsuke's principle in making friends was that the other person had to have talent.

units.source_text: 就算是品行端正的君子，如果对知识没有强烈的追求，对他来说都是没用的路人。

en.t: Even a morally upright gentleman, if he had no intense pursuit of knowledge, was to him nothing more than a useless passerby.

units.source_text: 他不要求朋友性情温和善良。

en.t: He did not require his friends to be gentle and kind by nature.

units.source_text: 即使他的朋友没有青年人的热情，他也觉得无所谓。

en.t: Even if his friends lacked the passion of youth, he did not mind.

units.source_text: 不，不如说所谓的好朋友让他觉得害怕。

en.t: No, rather, so-called good friends made him feel afraid.

units.source_text: 所以，他的朋友都一定得有头脑。

en.t: Therefore, all of his friends had to have intellect.

units.source_text: 头脑——一颗清晰的的头脑。

en.t: Intellect, a clear intellect.

units.source_text: 他喜欢头脑清晰的人胜过美少年。

en.t: He preferred people with clear minds to beautiful youths.

units.source_text: 与此同时，他憎恶头脑清楚的人胜过品行端正的君子。

en.t: At the same time, he hated people with clear minds more than morally upright gentlemen.

units.source_text: 事实上，他的友情常常都是在喜欢的热情里，掺杂这憎恶。

en.t: In fact, his friendships were often mixed with hatred within the passion of affection.

units.source_text: 直到现在，信辅依然觉得在这种热情之外没有友情。

en.t: Even now, Shinsuke still felt that there was no friendship outside such passion.

units.source_text: 他觉得至少在这种热情之外，没有不 Herr und Knecht（德语，直译为主仆关系）气味的友情。

en.t: He felt that, at least outside such passion, there was no friendship without the odor of Herr und Knecht, German for a master-servant relationship.

units.source_text: 况且他当时的朋友，从另一个方面说，正是与他势不两立的敌人。

en.t: Moreover, his friends at the time were, in another sense, enemies utterly opposed to him.

units.source_text: 他用自己的头脑当做武器，不断跟他们做斗争。

en.t: He used his own mind as a weapon and fought them constantly.

units.source_text: 惠特曼、自由诗、创造的进化——战场无处不在。

en.t: Whitman, free verse, creative evolution, the battlefield was everywhere.

units.source_text: 在战场上，他打败他的朋友们，或者被他的朋友们打败。

en.t: On that battlefield, he defeated his friends, or was defeated by them.

units.source_text: 这种精神上的战斗，毫无疑问成为了他通过杀戮获得喜悦的行为。

en.t: This spiritual combat undoubtedly became for him an act of finding joy through slaughter.

units.source_text: 然而，在这个过程里自然展现的新观念和新的美感形象也是毫无疑问的事实。

en.t: Yet it was also an undeniable fact that new ideas and new images of beauty naturally emerged in the process.

units.source_text: 凌晨三点的烛光是怎样照耀他们的辩论的？

en.t: How did the candlelight at three in the morning shine upon their debates?

units.source_text: 武者小路实笃的作品又是怎样支配他们的论战的？

en.t: And how did the works of Saneatsu Mushanokoji dominate their arguments?

units.source_text: 信辅还清楚的记得，在九月的某一个夜晚，有几只很大的飞蛾扑向了燃烧的蜡烛，绚丽夺目的飞蛾在黑夜中突然出现。

en.t: Shinsuke still clearly remembered one night in September when several large moths rushed toward the burning candle, and those dazzling moths suddenly appeared in the darkness.

units.source_text: 但是，一旦飞蛾扑火，也就不可思议的瞬间死去了。

en.t: But once the moths flew into the flame, they died in an unbelievably instant moment.

units.source_text: 可能这也不是什么大不了的事。

en.t: Perhaps this, too, was nothing very important.

units.source_text: 但是，信辅一直到今天，只要一想起这件小事——只要一想起那不可思议的美丽飞蛾的生死，不知道怎么回事，他的内心深处就会被孤寂占领……

en.t: But even today, whenever Shinsuke recalls this small incident, whenever he recalls the life and death of those mysteriously beautiful moths, somehow the depths of his heart are taken over by loneliness...
